headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Windsurf’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can expose Chatwoot customer data if paired without isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, while Windsurf reads workspace files, uses MCP, and accepts clipboard/file inputs. That creates a plausible injection bridge if Chatwoot content is copied into files or prompts that Windsurf treats as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into a Windsurf workspace file or clipboard prompt
IF Windsurf parses customer-authored text as instructions via MCP or file context
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw support transcripts into coding prompts
Use a redaction step before moving Chatwoot content into Windsurf
Restrict Windsurf to a separate workspace for non-customer data
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported text
requires-engineering: enforce prompt/content sanitization at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages; Windsurf has broad network egress, reads workspace files, and can use MCP servers. If customer data enters the shared workspace or prompts, Windsurf can transmit it outward. The pair therefore has a realistic exfiltration path in default use, with irreversible privacy impact.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records or messages are placed in a Windsurf-readable workspace
IF Windsurf sends those files or prompts through its model proxy or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot data out of the coding workspace
Use a separate OS account or directory for support data
Disable or tightly scope MCP servers for any workspace with customer data
Review outbound network destinations before running the pair
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on files copied from Chatwoot

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Chatwoot has broad network egress and customer-support workflows. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, Windsurf’s per-window shared state via local filesystem creates a direct write-conflict and corruption risk. The overlap is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents target the same local directory or git repository
IF Windsurf auto-executes edits while Chatwoot-driven artifacts are being updated
mitigations: Assign separate repositories or directories per agent
Turn off auto-execute in Windsurf for shared workspaces
Use git locks or a single-writer workflow
Pause one agent before the other writes to the same tree
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate support content and reports, and Windsurf can act on files and git state. If Chatwoot output is fed into Windsurf without verification, Windsurf may implement incorrect or maliciously shaped instructions. The pair is not inherently self-verifying, but the downstream blast radius is usually bounded to code/workspace changes.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated text is treated as authoritative task input by Windsurf
IF Windsurf applies edits or commits without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Separate factual support output from implementation tasks
Use checklists for any Chatwoot-derived action item
Limit Windsurf to read-only mode for imported instructions
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Windsurf handles open files and model-provider keys with broad egress. The profiles do not state residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated customer data is moved into Windsurf’s environment. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is copied into Windsurf-managed files or prompts
IF Windsurf’s model provider or MCP endpoints are outside the required residency or retention boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Windsurf prompts and files
Confirm retention and residency settings before use
Use synthetic or masked support cases for coding tasks
Document a data-handling boundary between support and coding tools
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency/retention
